question: Post-plant B Site Split 3v2, spike planted, 34s, DEF on semi-buy. You are KAY/O on site (Frag/ment, Flashdrive, Zero Point). How do you hold the post-plant?

options.label: Spread a crossfire B Main / B Heaven with your teammates and save Frag/ment for the defuse attempt
options.explication_courte: In a 3v2 with numbers advantage, a B Main (low) / B Heaven (high) crossfire forces the 2 DEF to choose between two angles; save the molly for the defuse moment.

options.label: Throw Zero Point to suppress DEF util before they engage on the retake
options.explication_courte: Suppressing DEF util before a forced retake is defensible, but against a semi-buy the 2 DEF have limited util anyway - the crossfire is more impactful than the knife here.

sources_option.citation: KAY/O's suppression is high-value to deny anchor or retake utility, but against a low-util semi-buy in a numbers-up post-plant the knife often reveals little and is better saved.

options.label: Stack all 3 on B Heaven to hold one strong vertical angle
options.explication_courte: Stacking all 3 on one angle leaves the other entry to the defuse unguarded: DEF can defuse through the uncovered axis with no resistance.

sources_option.citation: Covering only one approach in a post-plant leaves the opposite defuse angle open; spreading crossfires beats stacking a single sightline.

options.label: Push out toward the 2 DEF in B Main to finish the round on frags
options.explication_courte: Leaving post-plant in a 3v2 to chase frags gives unnecessary duels and frees the spike: you abandon your time leverage for a gamble.

sources_option.citation: In a numbers-up post-plant you win by holding stable angles and letting the clock run, not by pushing into the defenders and donating duels.

explication_longue:
Situation: 3v2 post-plant on B Site Split, spike planted, 34 seconds, DEF on semi-buy. You are KAY/O on site with Frag/ment, Flashdrive, Zero Point.

Post-plant with numbers advantage, three principles: (1) spread your players across distinct angles (never stack), (2) save your best delay util for the defuse moment, (3) let the DEF come to you. B Site Split has two main retake axes: B Main (low ground) and B Heaven (high ground). Three attackers must cover both - two bodies in a crossfire plus one off-angle watching the spike.

Correct sequence: crossfire B Main / B Heaven, save Frag/ment for the defuse sound, activate on defuse attempt. The 2 DEF cannot safely approach from either axis. Zero Point now (acceptable) strips their util but against a semi-buy they have little util to strip - the crossfire value is higher. Stacking B Heaven (costly) leaves B Main open. Pushing for frags (mistake) abandons leverage.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% crossfire + saved Frag/ment, ~22% Zero Point suppression first, ~16% Heaven stack (costly), ~6% push for frags (mistake).

sources.citation: On B Split the vertical B Heaven angle plus B Main ground access lets attackers set a two-height crossfire that defenders cannot challenge from a single position.
Attack post-plant means spreading out, playing off the spike, holding crossfires and using utility to delay the defuse rather than dumping it early.
Crossfires are the most consistent post-plant win condition; two players at distinct angles force a trade the defender can't isolate, especially when numbers-up.

_gaps.incertitude: Estimations depuis guides post-plant + Split (thunderpick, dignitas, boostroom) ; la frequence crossfire vs knife-first depend de la util DEF reelle en semi-buy, non fixee.
Le Zero Point (acceptable) peut monter optimal si les DEF gardent une util anchor forte malgre le semi-buy ; la frontiere depend de leur loadout non encode.
Positions x/y approximatives sur B Site Split (viewBox 1000x1000, zones de maps.ts) ; la hauteur exacte de B Heaven est un attribut de zone non geometrise dans le token 2D.
